A 3% fee that supports what’s next

The marketplace fee supports app maintenance and future development of Tari.

App maintenance

Keeping Tari Market running

The fee helps fund ongoing app maintenance, including upkeep, bug fixes, and improvements to the buying and selling experience.

Future development

Supporting Tari’s future

The fee also goes toward future development of Tari, supporting continued work on the ecosystem the marketplace is built on.

How it is calculated

3% of the item price

The buyer’s full payment enters escrow at purchase and is released only to the original seller or refunded to the original buyer. The seller pays the 3% item fee separately after a completed sale. Shipping is excluded from the separate fee. No additional 3% charge is added to the buyer’s checkout total.

For an item priced at 100 tTari with 10 tTari shipping, the buyer pays 110 tTari. Escrow releases all 110 tTari to the seller. The seller separately approves a 3 tTari fee payment.

Refunds & payment

Paid separately by the seller

No marketplace fee is taken when an order receives a full escrow refund. Network transaction fees are separate from this 3% fee.

The security and separate-fee upgrade is deployed on Esmeralda for testing. Existing orders follow the fee amounts recorded by their contract at purchase.

Payment & delivery

You are buying one item. The total includes the item price and seller-set shipping. Payment is in tTari.

As soon as your purchase transaction completes, the full item price plus shipping moves from your wallet into Ootle escrow. The funds stay there until receipt is confirmed, an eligible seller timeout claim is made, or an owner resolves a dispute. The seller can claim approximately 14 days after recorded purchase if there is no open dispute, even if delivery has not been recorded.

The updated buyer-confirmation flow requires a rating and written comment. The updated contract is deployed on Esmeralda for testing.

Shipping details are encrypted for the seller before a purchase is submitted. Network fees are separate from the order total; the wallet shows the transaction for your approval.

Your cases

Start a refund or dispute

Both actions open a case for owner review. Only orders still held in escrow are eligible.

Disputes & refunds

tTari is deposited into escrow at purchase. If an order goes wrong, a dispute keeps those funds held until a decision.

Choose your purchase, then approve the request in the wallet used to buy it.

01 · Check your order

Raise a problem before payment is released

If an item has not arrived, arrived damaged, or differs from its description, keep the order details and any relevant photos or tracking information. These are examples of issues to raise, not automatic grounds for a refund.

Do not confirm receipt while a problem remains unresolved: confirmation releases payment. Only the buyer’s wallet can open an order dispute, and only while its escrow remains unsettled.

02 · Open a dispute

Use your buying wallet

  1. Connect the Tari wallet used to purchase the item.
  2. Open Refunds & disputes and find the order under “Start a refund or dispute”.
  3. Select Open dispute.
  4. Approve the transaction in your wallet and wait for it to complete.

A declined or failed wallet transaction does not open a dispute. The current action records the disputed status; it does not submit a written explanation or attachments.

03 · Escrow pauses

The purchase payment stays locked

Once the dispute transaction completes, the order is marked disputed. Both buyer confirmation and the seller’s timeout claim are blocked until the marketplace owner resolves the dispute.

Simply contacting someone or saving evidence does not pause escrow. The dispute must be recorded before a release transaction settles.

04 · Marketplace decision

The owner resolves the dispute

The marketplace owner is the authorized decision-maker. Resolution requires an owner-signed transaction choosing a full buyer refund or payment to the seller. Neither party can unilaterally take disputed funds.

Keep the order ID, purchase transaction, item description, delivery tracking, photos, and any correspondence available for review. Evidence uploads are not built into this app. The marketplace owner can review pending cases and submit the decision in Admin disputes after connecting the owner wallet.

There is no automatic decision deadline or guaranteed refund. A dispute stays pending until the owner resolves it.

Outcome A · Refund approved

The full escrow amount returns to the buyer

The contract sends the order’s full tTari payment—including item price and shipping—to the buyer’s refund wallet address recorded at purchase. No marketplace fee is deducted from that refund.

For a 100 tTari item with 10 tTari shipping, the refund is 110 tTari. The refund is in tTari test funds, which have no monetary value. Network transaction fees are separate and are not returned from the escrow balance.

Check the completed transaction and your wallet balance to verify receipt. This flow does not support partial refunds.

Outcome B · Seller payment approved

Escrow releases to the seller

If the owner resolves the dispute in the seller’s favor, the upgraded contract releases the full escrow payment to the original seller. Any marketplace fee is paid separately by the seller. The order is then settled.

The security upgrade releases the full payment to the original seller. The 3% item fee is a separate seller-approved payment. Existing orders use the fee amounts recorded by their contract at purchase.

Timing & returns

Understand the limits

Without an open dispute, the seller can submit a payment claim after 1,008 epochs—approximately 14 days—from recorded purchase. Open a dispute promptly if there is a problem; do not assume the funds are still held after that window.

Once the order has been released or refunded, this contract cannot reopen its dispute or reverse settlement. There is no built-in appeal, return-label service, return-shipping reimbursement, or automatic change-of-mind cancellation.

A return arrangement is separate from the on-chain refund action. The app currently does not track returned goods or enforce return conditions.

Ratings & feedback

A review dispute is different

Disputing a rating or comment asks the owner to review public seller feedback. It does not open a payment dispute, freeze escrow, or refund a purchase.

Refunded orders do not receive seller ratings. The pending automatic-review feature applies only to successful, undisputed timeout claims; an open payment dispute prevents that claim.

How Ootle escrow works

Follow your tTari payment from checkout to the seller—or back to you if a refund is approved.

Esmeralda testnet testing

The new marketplace is deployed. Listings, purchases, usernames, and disputes are open for testing with test funds. Existing orders retain their original contract rules.

01 · Checkout

tTari enters escrow at purchase

You approve the item price plus shipping in tTari through your Tari wallet. When the purchase transaction completes, that full amount immediately enters the Ootle marketplace contract’s escrow vault. The purchase and escrow deposit complete together. The funds remain there until the order is released or refunded. Payment is in tTari.

Your wallet may also charge a network transaction fee, separate from the order total.

02 · Shipping

The seller sends your item

The seller marks the order shipped. Your name and shipping address are encrypted in your browser for the seller before they accompany the order.

The payment is already in escrow while the seller ships your item. The marketplace owner records carrier-confirmed delivery, for tracking. The seller’s 14-day claim window starts at purchase. Recording delivery does not reset the clock or move funds.

03 · Buyer confirmation

Confirm after checking your item

Use your recent orders to confirm receipt after the item arrives and you have checked it.

Receipt confirmation: confirmation requires a 1–5 star rating and a written comment. Confirmation, feedback, and payment release complete together in one transaction.

04 · Purchase window

If the buyer does not respond

After 1,008 network epochs—approximately 14 days from recorded purchase—the seller can claim payment if the order has no open dispute. The seller must submit the claim; the clock alone does not move the funds.

Automatic review: a successful timeout claim adds 5 stars and “Sale Satisfactory” when no buyer review exists. The review is labeled automatic.

If something goes wrong

Disputes and refunds

The buyer can open a dispute before payment is released. An open dispute blocks buyer confirmation and the seller’s timeout claim.

The marketplace owner decides whether to refund the buyer or release payment to the seller. An approved refund returns the full escrowed item and shipping amount, with no marketplace fee. Network transaction fees are separate.

A dispute does not guarantee a refund. Once escrow has settled, this contract’s dispute flow cannot reverse it.

Terms, privacy & risks

Before you use Tari Market.

Tari Market is a lawful-goods marketplace. You may use it only when every part of a listing or transaction—including the product, payment, possession, shipment, import, and export—is legal.

Esmeralda testnet only. Use test funds, fictional shipping details, and test listings. Do not send real goods or funds. End-to-end testing is in progress; this demo is not a production-ready marketplace.

If an item or transaction is illegal anywhere connected to the sale, do not list it, buy it, sell it, ship it, or pay for it here.

Prohibited activity and products include

  • Illegal drugs, controlled substances, unlawful drug paraphernalia, and prescription products sold without required authorization.
  • Firearms, ammunition, explosives, weapons, defense articles, or other dangerous or regulated items prohibited by law or Tari Market policy.
  • Stolen, counterfeit, pirated, fraudulent, unsafe, recalled, or intellectual-property-infringing goods.
  • Human trafficking or exploitation, sexual services, child sexual abuse material, and any abusive or non-consensual material.
  • Fraud, money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions or embargo evasion, trade in criminal proceeds, and attempts to conceal unlawful conduct.
  • Any other product or service whose listing, sale, ownership, transport, import, export, or payment violates applicable law.

Your responsibility

You are responsible for complying with all applicable U.S. federal, state, tribal, territorial, and local laws, and every applicable foreign and international rule. This includes sanctions and embargoes, customs and export controls, taxes, licensing, age restrictions, product-safety and consumer-protection requirements, intellectual-property rights, and carrier or shipping restrictions. Do not transact if you are unsure whether it is lawful.

Risk of loss and limitation of responsibility

Transactions and shipments are between buyers and sellers. Tari Market will make reasonable efforts to help users investigate and resolve reported problems, but it cannot guarantee delivery, recovery, refund, replacement, return, or restoration of any goods or tTari that are lost, stolen, damaged, misdirected, inaccessible, or otherwise unrecoverable. To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, Tari Market and its operator are not responsible or legally liable for such losses. This limitation does not exclude or limit liability that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.

Enforcement and cooperation

Privacy features and cryptocurrency do not provide immunity from the law. Tari Market may reject or remove listings, restrict access, preserve relevant records, report suspected illegal activity, and respond to valid legal process where permitted or required by law.

Marketplace role & seller duties

The seller is responsible for the listing, authority to sell, accurate descriptions, lawful delivery, and applicable taxes and product obligations. Tari Market provides the interface and contract-based payment workflow; it does not inspect, authenticate, insure, or guarantee goods. A wallet connection or seller rating is not identity verification. Do not use another person’s wallet, manipulate reviews, or submit misleading listings. Sellers must honor applicable shipment, cancellation, and refund requirements; the escrow timer does not replace those duties.

Escrow timing — read before purchasing

The full item price plus shipping enters escrow when the purchase succeeds. Buyer confirmation releases payment and requires a rating and written comment. Without an open dispute, the seller can claim payment after 1,008 epochs (approximately 14 days) from recorded purchase, even if delivery has not been recorded. This is a purchase-based window, not 14 days after delivery. “Protected by escrow” describes this limited holding mechanism; it is not insurance or guaranteed buyer protection. Monitor your order and open a dispute before settlement if there is a problem.

Disputes, evidence & refund limits

Only the buying wallet can open an unsettled order dispute. A failed or declined transaction does not open a case. An open dispute blocks buyer confirmation and seller timeout claims until an authorized owner decision. The owner chooses a full refund to the original buyer or full release to the original seller. Refunds include the escrowed item price and shipping, but not separately paid network fees. Refunds are in tTari, not a guaranteed dollar value. Partial refunds, appeals, return labels, return tracking, and conditional returns are not built in. A feedback dispute does not freeze payment. Keep transaction IDs, descriptions, tracking, photos, and correspondence; this demo has no evidence-upload channel or guaranteed response deadline. Owner unavailability or loss of owner-wallet access can leave disputed funds locked indefinitely. Do not place private evidence in public listings or reviews.

Fees & Tari references

All current payments and fees use tTari test funds, which have no monetary value. For the current payment flow, the seller separately approves a fee of 3% of the item price after a completed sale; shipping is excluded. The buyer pays no additional 3% checkout surcharge. Full escrow refunds do not incur this marketplace fee. Network fees are separate and may still be incurred for transactions that do not produce a successful purchase. Older orders follow their recorded contract terms. The stated fee purpose is app maintenance and future Tari ecosystem development. This demo does not publish an allocation percentage, beneficiary commitment, or remittance schedule for ecosystem funding. The fee is not represented as a charitable donation. Use of Tari technology does not by itself establish Tari sponsorship, endorsement, or a guarantee.

Wallet, network & software risks

Review the network, account, amount, destination, and transaction in your wallet before approving. Never provide seed phrases or private wallet keys to this website or to someone claiming to offer support. Bugs, attacks, compromised devices, lost keys, network delays, outages, or testnet resets can cause permanent loss or inaccessibility. Transactions may be irreversible and a completed settlement cannot be reopened through this contract. tTari has no monetary value. No uninterrupted availability, error-free software, investment return, or independently audited security is promised. Disconnecting a wallet does not reverse prior approvals or transactions.

Privacy — information used by the app

The interface processes connected wallet/account identifiers, listings, seller profiles, reviews, order details, transaction IDs, and shipping fields to display the market and support purchases and fulfillment. Treat listings, profiles, reviews, wallet identifiers, and on-chain transaction information as potentially public and linkable. Do not include personal information in public content. Shipping details are encrypted in the browser for the seller before purchase submission; the encrypted payload is included in the order workflow. The seller can decrypt those details and may retain or share them for fulfillment. Encryption does not guarantee anonymity, prevent seller misuse, or protect a compromised device.

Privacy — storage, providers & deletion

Browser storage keeps preferences, cached listings/rates, order history, and wallet-session information; seller delivery decryption keys are held in this browser’s IndexedDB. The acceptance record is session-local, not a wallet signature or a durable server consent record. The app contacts hosting infrastructure, the Tari indexer/network, CoinGecko for reference prices, and WalletConnect/Reown when that connection method is used. Those providers may receive IP addresses, request metadata, and connection information under their own policies. The local-wallet option communicates with your configured local wallet service. Clearing browser site data removes local records but may also destroy delivery decryption keys; it does not erase blockchain records or copies retained by sellers or providers. This demo does not offer an automated data-access/deletion request channel or a fixed retention schedule across those parties. Never submit real personal or shipping information during testing.

Consumer rights & notice changes

Nothing here waives non-excludable consumer, privacy, or other statutory rights, excuses unlawful conduct, or removes duties imposed on the operator or sellers. Technical finality is not a ruling on legal entitlement to a refund or other remedy. This notice does not impose mandatory arbitration or a class-action waiver. Material updates will carry a new notice version and require acknowledgment again; website wording cannot retroactively change an existing order’s contract mechanics. Operator legal identity, a dedicated contact channel, and production dispute-service commitments must be established before real-world trading is offered.

Important: This notice is not legal advice and does not guarantee that a listing or transaction is lawful. A disclaimer cannot replace identity and seller controls, listing review, reporting systems, sanctions screening, or advice from qualified counsel.

Create a separate test wallet here. On return visits, this site recognizes the saved wallet and asks you to unlock it. No extension or local launcher is needed.
